preregistration.expectation: Killing agent-browser's background daemon mid-session will either resume the prior page or start fresh; a 5-site public sample (reduced from the 'about 10' in the next_check, time-boxed) will mostly succeed for both tools; Playwright, being process-per-invocation with no daemon, has no equivalent daemon-kill scenario.
preregistration.criteria: Record daemon PID before/after SIGKILL, whether 'get title' after relaunch reflects the pre-kill page, whether owned Chrome processes are cleaned up, and per-site pass/fail/latency for agent-browser and Playwright on 5 public sites.

playwright_kill_recovery_control.purpose: FIX ROUND: the review noted the original receipt skipped a Playwright kill-and-recover half as having 'no analog'. Playwright's architecture (process-per-invocation, no daemon) really has no daemon to kill, but a comparable control -- SIGKILL the node process mid-task and observe cleanup/rerun -- was possible and is run here.
playwright_kill_recovery_control.script: scripts/pw_kill_test.mjs (opens the loopback fixture, fills #name, then waits 15s before clicking -- SIGKILL sent during the wait)
playwright_kill_recovery_control.post_kill_process_check: `ps -p <killed pid>` returned no matching process immediately after `kill -9`; a `ps aux | grep chrom` count taken right after the kill was 0 -- no orphaned Chrome child processes survived this SIGKILL (raw/pw_kill_ps_after_kill.log)
playwright_kill_recovery_control.rerun_result: A fresh `node pw_kill_test.mjs` invocation immediately after completed normally end-to-end: `{"finished":true,"status":"Hello, Kill Test!"}` (raw/pw_kill_rerun_stdout.log) -- as expected for a stateless, process-per-invocation tool, the rerun has no prior state to recover and simply redoes the whole task.
playwright_kill_recovery_control.caveat: pw_kill_test.mjs itself does not call browser.close() at the end, so on the (non-killed) rerun the node process and its Chromium tree kept running after printing output until manually pkilled a few seconds later -- an artifact of this test script omitting cleanup, not a finding about Playwright's kill/recovery behavior. This is unrelated to the mid-task-kill result above, which measured process state immediately after the SIGKILL, not after a clean run.

results.site_sample_tally_fix_round: FIX ROUND correction: the README/outcome_detail originally read '5/5 pass each'. Of the 5 sites, https://httpstat.us/200 returned a page titled '404 Not Found' for both tools despite the URL asking for a 200 -- almost certainly httpstat.us-side flakiness, not a tool defect, but it is not a clean pass either. Corrected tally: 4/5 clear passes plus 1/5 indeterminate (site-side anomaly) for each tool. Separately, the Wikipedia row (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Random) is not a fixed, repeatable sample: by design it redirects to a different random article on every request, so agent-browser landed on 'Scott Porter (rugby league)' and Playwright landed on 'Slovakia men's national ball hockey team' -- two different pages, not the same page loaded twice. Both tools still successfully loaded *a* Wikipedia article, which is the property actually being tested (arbitrary-site compatibility), so this does not change the tally, but the two runs are not comparable page-for-page.

outcome_detail: Narrows but does not fully settle the gap; corrected during the fix round from an overstated 5/5-pass tally. Crash-recovery: the agent-browser daemon auto-relaunches on next command but does NOT restore prior page/session state by default (restore is 'not_configured'), and the original run reported that killing the daemon orphaned owned Chrome child processes rather than closing them as documented -- however no raw log for that specific sequence was retained (see raw_evidence_caveat), so treat the exact PIDs/count as unverified-but-plausible. A new, retained-log control on Playwright (SIGKILL mid-task, not a daemon-kill since Playwright has none) shows a cleaner result: 0 orphaned Chrome processes immediately after the kill, and a stateless fresh rerun completes normally -- a real architectural contrast (agent-browser's persistent daemon has cleanup edge cases; Playwright's process-per-invocation model has none to have) even though the two are not the same kind of kill test. Site compatibility: agent-browser and Playwright each cleanly passed 4 of 5 sites (example.com, a Wikipedia article, iana.org, playwright.dev); the 5th, httpstat.us/200, returned an anomalous '404 Not Found' page for both tools and is counted as indeterminate, not a pass, for either. The Wikipedia:Random URL is not a fixed sample (each tool landed on a different random article), which is expected of that URL and does not undermine the compatibility result, but is noted for reproducibility.
limits: Time-boxed to 5 public sites, not the ~10 in next_check; this is a reduced, not full, compatibility sample.
The tally is 4/5 clear passes + 1/5 indeterminate per tool, not 5/5; see site_sample_tally_fix_round.
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Random is not a fixed/repeatable URL (each request lands on a different article); the two tools were not tested against the same page.

The original agent-browser daemon-kill numbers (PIDs, 8 orphaned processes, restoreStatus) have no retained raw log in the repo or the cache dir; they are reported as originally observed, not re-verified in this fix round. A retained-log Playwright SIGKILL control was added instead (playwright_kill_recovery_control) as the closest thing to a like-for-like kill test, since Playwright has no daemon to kill.
The scope of the original 'pkilled manually' Chrome cleanup (this namespace only vs. host-wide) was not recorded.
Did not test the file-protocol rejection mentioned in the original gap text; loopback HTTP was used throughout.

Reproducibility: scripts/pw_sites.mjs and scripts/pw_kill_test.mjs are committed; raw/ab_sites_results.json, raw/pw_sites_results.json, raw/pw_kill_prekill_stderr.log, raw/pw_kill_ps_after_kill.log and raw/pw_kill_rerun_stdout.log are the retained raw outputs for this receipt.
